olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
(a) Suppose that each square of a $4\times7$ chessboard is colored either black or white. Prove that with any such coloring, the board must contain a rectangle (formed by the horizontal and vertical lines of the board) whose four distinct corner squares are all of the same color.

(b) Exhibit a black-white coloring of a $4\times6$ board in which the four corner squares of every rectangle are not all of the same color.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If $A$ and $B$ are fixed points on a given circle and $XY$ is a variable diameter of the same circle, determine the locus of the point of intersection of lines $AX$ and $BY$. You may assume that $AB$ is not a diameter.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If the sum of the lengths of the six edges of a trirectangular tetrahedron $PABC$ (i.e., $\angle APB=\angle BPC=\angle CPA=90^\circ$) is $S$, determine its maximum volume.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
If $P(x)$, $Q(x)$, $R(x)$, and $S(x)$ are polynomials such that
$$P(x^5)+xQ(x^5)+x^2R(x^5)=(x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1)S(x),$$
prove that $x-1$ is a factor of $P(x)$.
